title: Dual Queue Effect Scheduler (Layout Sync vs Passive Async)
concept: Scheduler Separation of Layout and Passive Effect Queues
problemStatement: Implement `createEffectScheduler()` that maintains two effect queues: `layoutQueue` (executed synchronously during commit) and `passiveQueue` (executed asynchronously after a tick). Returns an object with `scheduleLayout(fn)`, `schedulePassive(fn)`, `flushLayout()`, and `flushPassive()`.
interviewTrap: If layout effects throw errors, the commit fails synchronously. If passive effects throw errors, they are surfaced in the next turn of the event loop.

testCases.name: Executes layout effects synchronously before passive effects
testCases.testFn: const s = createEffectScheduler(); const log = []; s.schedulePassive(() => log.push('passive')); s.scheduleLayout(() => log.push('layout')); s.flushLayout(); await s.flushPassive(); return log;

testCases.name: flushLayout clears all pending layout items
testCases.testFn: const s = createEffectScheduler(); s.scheduleLayout(() => 1); s.scheduleLayout(() => 2); return s.flushLayout();

testCases.name: flushPassive runs asynchronously after tick
testCases.input: passive flush resolves with executed values
testCases.testFn: const s = createEffectScheduler(); s.schedulePassive(() => 'async-done'); return await s.flushPassive();

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: A Dual Queue Effect Scheduler implements the two-tiered queuing architecture used by React: A Synchronous Layout Queue (processed immediately during commit) and an Asynchronous Passive Queue (processed in a microtask or message channel after paint).
stepByStepWalkthrough: - Synchronously drains and executes all effects in `layoutQueue`.
- Schedules asynchronous draining of `passiveQueue` via `setTimeout(flushPassive, 0)` or `postMessage`.
Verify that layout effects always execute before passive effects, even if scheduled in reverse order.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React source code (`packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberWorkLoop.js`), `commitRoot` processes `commitLayoutEffects` directly. It then requests scheduling for `flushPassiveEffects` via `Scheduler_scheduleCallback(NormalSchedulerPriority, () => flushPassiveEffects())`.

complexity.time: O(L) synchronous layout flush + O(P) asynchronous passive flush.
complexity.space: O(L + P) queue storage for scheduled effect thunks.

edgeCasesHandled: Strict priority guarantee: all layout effects finish before any passive effect starts.
Clean draining: queues are emptied upon execution.
Asynchronous passive execution allows browser paint tick in between.

specifications: React Architecture: The Passive Effects Queue implementation
verifiedRules: Layout effects are flushed synchronously during the commit phase.
Passive effects are deferred to allow paint and prevent frame drops.
